Vuelta 2026: Results

fotobureau Cor VosMikel Landa won the 20th stage and Enric Mas retained the lead in the general classification. There is one stage remaining in the 81st edition of the Vuelta a España, with the race finishing on a city circuit in Granada. Every day, you’ll find results, race reports, videos and more on Cyclingstage.com.

Top 3 Vuelta 2026

1. Enric Mas
2. Primoz Roglic + 2:15
3. Felix Gall + 2:44

Another interesting read: winners and records Vuelta a España.

Via the links in the table below, you can access the results, race reports and overall classification.

Landa solos to victory, Mas seals GC

The Vuelta’s queen stage is action-packed from the very start. Eventually, Mikel Landa drops his fellow attackers, Ramses Debruyne and Tobias Halland Johannessen, early on the final climb, and the veteran powers his way to a commanding victory on the brutally steep sections. Enric Mas finishes almost 7 minutes later to secure overall victory.
Read more »

Dunbar conquers Peñas Blancas, Mas retains red

With 2 kilometres to go on the final climb, Santiago Buitrago rides away from his breakaway companions Thomas Gloag, Eddie Dunbar and Urko Berrade. The Irishman comes back to him inside the final 500 metres and rides straight past him. Dunbar takes the spoils, while GC contenders finish together, with Enric Mas retaining the red jersey.
Read more »

Küng storms to glory, Mas retains lead

Stefan Küng claims victory in the individual time trial from El Puerto de Santa María to Jerez de la Frontera, finishing ahead of Callum Thornley and João Almeida. Enric Mas retains the red jersey, while Primož Roglič moves up to second overall at Felix Gall’s expense.
Read more »

Brennan strikes again, Mas retains red

Matthew Brennan takes his fifth stage win in the flattest stage of La Vuelta, outsprinting Jordi Meeus and Magnus Cort on the line. Enric Mas retains the overall lead.
Read more »

Brennan powers to his fourth win, Mas still lead

From the outset, the riders are heading for a sprint finish on stage 16. Visma | Lease a Bike controls the peloton throughout the day, before Wout van Aert delivers a perfect lead-out for Matthew Brennan. The Brit says thank you by finishing it off in convincing fashion. Enric Mas retains the red jersey.
